stem: For Confucius, names had ____ contents, no matter how time marched on and the affairs of the world changed, the proper names of things absolutely could not vary.

Astronomy dominated ancient science partly because it was ____ in a way that the physics and biology of the time were not: even in prehistory, people probably used the apparent motion of the Sun, for example, as a crude clock, calendar, and compass.

An architect of Koolhaas’ (i)____ might plausibly prefer designing on paper to building in concrete. Remaining within the realm of his own imagination, he need not worry about pesky clients who can dilute a project into mediocrity. But in fact, what Koolhaas enjoys most is the opportunity to engage with a client. When asked if he would consider designing a house for himself, he replied that the idea bored him, that it would feel too (ii)____. For him, the whole point of architecture is the encounter with the other.

Belief in the harmful effects of the drug has all the hallmarks of a viewpoint that is not (i)____ even though the notion that the drug has negative consequences has been (ii)____ multiple epidemiological studies over the past decade. Yet the true believers have (iii)____, critiquing each new study that challenges their views and continuing to lean on supporting research that was retracted long ago.
She criticizes the view that American democracy is ____, its strings pulled not by voters but by a power elite or ruling class.

Until fairly recently, hitchhiking was not an uncommon practice in the United States, but today's motorists are likely to see the occasional hitchhiker as ____, thinking “l didn’t know people still did that!”
Legal scholars envision environmental politics as the pursuit of opposing and ____ interests and therefore likely to lead to confrontation rather than compromise.
